To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we can train deep networks, in a fully unsupervised fashion, by predicting noise.

(i) a simple unsupervised learning framework, based on predicting a fixed set of NATs, can be applied to any deep network, (ii) it produces representations on par with state of the art, (iii) it is scalable to large datasets, and (iv) it can be used for unsupervised domain adaptation.
we propose a novel approach to unsupervised learning, which we call Noise As Targets, and which is based on the idea of predicting the noise of the training data.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following questions: 1) How can we learn deep features with no supervision? 2) How can we make unsupervised feature learning robust?
a fundamental problem in computer vision: how to obtain visual representations from data without supervision?
the following two questions: (i) Can we train deep networks end-to-end without labels? (ii) Can we use a single model for different computer vision tasks?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
our method is able to produce features that perform on par or better than state-of-the-art features, without supervision.
the proposed method is able to learn representations that are competitive with state-of-the art unsupervised methods, and that are comparable to supervised methods, but with no labels.
this paper proposes a novel and generic framework to train unsupervised deep neural networks.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, we propose an unsupervised approach to train deep convolutional neural networks by predicting the noise.
we show how to train convolutional networks with no supervision.
we can train a deep neural network to learn representations of the data without any labels, just by using a fixed set of target representations (NAT).
The main takeaway from our work is that
the same deep network architecture can be used to learn representations with and without supervision.
deep features are able to learn meaningful visual representations by aligning to NATs that are not necessarily visually interpretable.
unsupervised deep learning can be achieved by predicting the noise in the data, and that it can be used as a building block for other unsupervised learning tasks.
